title: Maximum XOR After Operations
statement:
You have an integer array `nums`. One operation chooses an index `i` and any non-negative integer `x` and replaces `nums[i]` by `nums[i] AND (nums[i] XOR x)`, with AND and XOR meaning the bitwise operators.

You may perform as many operations as you like, including none. Return the largest possible value of the bitwise XOR of all the elements of `nums` afterwards.
notes:
## Intuition

First work out what one operation can do. Since `x` is free, `nums[i] XOR x` can be made equal to any value `y`, so the new value is `nums[i] AND y`: any number whose set bits are a subset of `nums[i]`'s bits. Operations can therefore clear bits but never create them.

Look at the final XOR one bit at a time. A bit that no element has can never appear. A bit that at least one element has can always be made to appear: keep it in exactly one element and clear it in the others, so it is set an odd number of times. Bits do not interfere, because each element can clear any subset of its bits independently. So every bit present anywhere can be set, and the answer is the bitwise OR of all elements.

A brute force would try every submask of every element, which is exponential.

## Approach

1. Start `answer` at 0.
2. For each `num` in `nums`, merge its bits into `answer` with `|=`.
3. Return `answer`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [3, 2, 4, 6]`, in binary `011, 010, 100, 110`.

- After 3: `answer = 011` (3).
- After 2: still `011` (3).
- After 4: `111` (7).
- After 6: still `111` (7).

The answer is `7`, which the original XOR (`3 ^ 2 ^ 4 ^ 6 = 3`) misses because bits 1 and 2 appear an even number of times.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n), one OR per element.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Returning the XOR of the original array ignores the operations; `[7, 7]` gives 0 instead of 7.
- The operation cannot add bits, so the answer is never larger than the OR; do not search for anything bigger.
- `nums[i] = 0` contributes nothing, and an all-zero array answers 0.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `answer` | OR of the elements seen so far: every bit that can be made odd |
| `num` | the current element |

narration.1: An operation can only clear bits of nums[i], and it can clear any subset of them.
narration.2: answer collects the bits that the final XOR can have.
narration.4: Any bit this element has can be kept here alone and cleared elsewhere, so it can be set in the XOR.
narration.5: Now answer holds every bit that appears in at least one element.
narration.6: No operation creates bits, so this OR is the largest reachable XOR.
